title: Imports and Dependencies
content: Imports Mathlib tactics, natural numbers, and real numbers. The real number library is essential here because the conjecture involves constants $C > 0$ in the bounds $R(G,T_n) \le Cn$ and $R(G,K_n) \le Cn^2$, which are naturally expressed as real-valued inequalities.
mathContext: Uses $\mathbb{N}$ for vertex counts and graph sizes, $\mathbb{R}$ for the linear/quadratic bound constants $C$ in $R(G,T_n) \le Cn$ and $R(G,K_n) \le Cn^2$.

title: Simple Graph on Fin n
content: Defines a simple graph on $n$ vertices as a symmetric, irreflexive adjacency relation on $\text{Fin}\;n$. This is the same graph representation used in Problems #566 and #567, providing consistency across the size Ramsey problem cluster.

title: Edge Counting
content: Counts edges by filtering ordered pairs $(u,v)$ with $u < v$ and adjacent. The ordering constraint avoids double-counting. This function is used both in the tree characterization ($|E(T)| = n-1$) and in the size linearity definition ($\hat{r}(G,H) \le C \cdot |E(H)|$).

title: No Isolated Vertices
content: Requires every vertex to have at least one neighbor. This condition appears in the conclusion of the conjecture: Ramsey size linearity is stated for opponents $H$ with no isolated vertices, ensuring the edge-based bound $\hat{r}(G,H) \le C \cdot |E(H)|$ is nontrivial.

title: Classical Ramsey Number (Axiomatized)
content: The classical Ramsey number $R(G,H)$ is the smallest $N$ such that every 2-coloring of $K_N$ contains a red $G$ or blue $H$. Axiomatized since the full construction requires existence proofs from Ramsey's theorem. This is the **classical** notion — the conjecture asks whether growth rates of $R(G, \cdot)$ control the **size** variant $\hat{r}(G, \cdot)$.
mathContext: $R(G,H) = \min\{N : K_N \to (G,H)\}$, where $K_N \to (G,H)$ means every 2-coloring of $E(K_N)$ yields a monochromatic $G$ or $H$.

title: Size Ramsey Number (Axiomatized)
content: The size Ramsey number $\hat{r}(G,H)$ is the smallest $m$ such that some graph $F$ with $m$ edges has the property that every 2-coloring of $E(F)$ yields a monochromatic $G$ or $H$. The key distinction from $R(G,H)$: the classical number minimizes **vertices** (via $K_N$), while the size number minimizes **edges** (via arbitrary $F$). The crude bound $\hat{r}(G,H) \le \binom{R(G,H)}{2}$ follows from taking $F = K_{R(G,H)}$.

title: Tree Characterization
content: A tree on $n \ge 1$ vertices is characterized by having exactly $n - 1$ edges. This simplified characterization (omitting connectedness) suffices for the conjecture, which quantifies over all trees. Trees represent the **sparsest** connected graphs and serve as one extreme in the hypothesis.
mathContext: $T$ is a tree $\iff |E(T)| = |V(T)| - 1$ (for connected $T$). Trees satisfy $R(T_m, T_n) = m + n - 2$ by Chvátal-Harary.

title: Complete Graph Predicate
content: A complete graph $K_n$ has all $\binom{n}{2}$ edges. Complete graphs represent the **densest** graphs and serve as the other extreme in the hypothesis. The classical Ramsey number $R(K_m, K_n)$ grows exponentially ($2^{\Theta(n)}$ for diagonal case), so a quadratic bound $R(G, K_n) \le Cn^2$ is a strong structural constraint implying $G$ is far from a clique.
mathContext: $K_n$ has $\binom{n}{2}$ edges. For diagonal Ramsey: $2^{n/2} \le R(K_n, K_n) \le 4^n$. Quadratic $R(G, K_n)$ requires $G$ to be sparse.

title: Linear Tree Ramsey Condition
content: The condition $R(G, T_n) \le Cn$ for all trees $T_n$ on $n$ vertices. This is a natural condition: by the Chvátal-Harary theorem, $R(T_m, T_n) = m + n - 2$, so trees themselves satisfy linear tree Ramsey trivially. More generally, graphs with bounded degeneracy or bounded bandwidth tend to have linear Ramsey numbers against trees. This condition captures that $G$ is 'tree-like' in Ramsey-theoretic terms.

title: Quadratic Clique Ramsey Condition
content: The condition $R(G, K_n) \le Cn^2$ for all complete graphs $K_n$. Since $R(K_m, K_n)$ grows exponentially, a polynomial bound is highly restrictive. The quadratic rate $O(n^2)$ is achieved by bounded-degree graphs (by the Chvátal-Rödl-Szemerédi-Trotter theorem). Together with linear tree Ramsey, this condition captures graphs that are well-behaved against both extremes of graph density.

title: Ramsey Size Linearity
content: The conclusion of the conjecture: $G$ is Ramsey size linear if $\hat{r}(G, H) \le C \cdot |E(H)|$ for all $H$ without isolated vertices. This is the same definition as in Problems #566 and #567. The conjecture asks whether the **classical** conditions (linear tree Ramsey + quadratic clique Ramsey) are sufficient to guarantee this **size** property.

title: EFRS Conjecture: Classical Bounds Imply Size Linearity
content: The central conjecture of Problem #568: if $G$ satisfies both $R(G, T_n) = O(n)$ for all trees and $R(G, K_n) = O(n^2)$ for all cliques, then $G$ is Ramsey size linear. This would establish a **bridge between classical and size Ramsey theory**: the growth rates of $R(G, \cdot)$ at two extremes (sparse trees and dense cliques) would control the edge-based quantity $\hat{r}(G, \cdot)$. The axiom form reflects the open status.
